title: The four-piece band at Tom Anderson's and its successors
summary: The four-piece band was later enlarged; Nicholas, Willie Santiago and Paul Barbarin followed; the cabaret used entertainers and written arrangements.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yeah, my name, my wife's name, and Paul Dominguez. Paul is dead. We had four pieces there.

One time I saw one picture of a band there, I think Wooden Joe had that picture. Who was that? Wooden Joe Nicholas. Oh, I know Wooden Joe, yeah. With his nephew who was playing, Barney Begard and Nicholas. Albert Nicholas. Albert Nicholas.
Albert Nicholas. They was playing Tom Anderson after we left there.
After the job, after you left. Yeah, yeah. I know Albert Nicholas.
I played many jobs with him. Oh, Willie San Diego, they had him on guitar.
He was a guitar player. Played with him too.
And I believe Paul Bartman was a drummer then after you left.
Paul Bartman, yeah, yeah, yeah. Yeah, yeah. That was after our time. Yeah. We were there first.
They had a little bit bigger band. You only had four pieces there.
Four pieces, yeah. That band was larger now.
See that time, but after the cabaret started getting plentiful, but they had competition, you had to increase the band, you see. What kind of place was that? Did they have any shows?
No, they had entertainers. Entertainers that sang all around the same place.

Yeah, we had four people. The fellow would take and raise the music and the corner play, he played on special chorus. Played the saxophone part. We'd write a lot for him, you see, with our four pieces. Because Louie would do it too. They would get a piano part and write the whole four pieces out. Yeah. Because Paul Lomengus, he was a good reader too. I know how much why. He was first class. But many of these fellows, they couldn't read too much. Yeah. But if they hear something, they can play it good the fellow read it though. One thing about them.
A wonderful ear of some of those people.
